Definition: a primary verb; to be of interest to, i.e. to concern (only third person singular present indicative used impersonally, it matters):--(take) care.
BiblicalUsage: Melo means to care, to be of interest to someone, and it is almost always used of God or of Jesus caring when no one else does. Matthew 22:16 has the Pharisees admit that Jesus carest for no man, and Mark 4:38 has the disciples cry, Master, carest thou not that we perish? 1 Peter 5:7 answers them both: cast all your care upon Him, for He careth for you.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the question the disciples asked in the storm is the question every frightened heart asks, and Peter's answer is the one that holds.
